messages:
Sasha: Heads up — after yesterday's perf regression (higher p50 on text-generation), we need a concrete plan for safe production profiling. We need low-overhead options + a fallback for deeper traces. Thoughts?

Juan: I captured a short nsys run from the repro window. Full API+kernel tracing added ~40% token latency (saw queueing spikes). Sampling runs look much cheaper (~5-12%), but they miss short-lived kernel hotspots.

Megan: Important distinction: "sampling" here = profiler sampling of PC stacks (captures hotspots) vs "instrumentation" which records every kernel/API call (CUPTI hooks). Instrumentation gives exact timelines but can blow up request latency and memory.

Liam: Agree. For safe-prod we should: 1) default to sampling (low freq, phasic), 2) allow short bounded full traces triggered by anomaly, 3) limit per-run duration/events. Also add NN-specific filters (only trace large-batch/long-seq requests).

perf-bot: nsys quick example (dev only):
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-frequency=1000 \
  --output=dev_trace --duration=20
```
Notes: sample-frequency here is illustrative — we tuned between 500-2000 Hz in experiments.

Juan: From our experiments:
- Sampling 1kHz, 20s window: overhead ~6-10%, enough to see kernel hotspots on 95%ile longer ops.
- Full trace (nvtx + cuda + cudnn) 20s: overhead ~30-50%, trace size x10-x50 and some traces OOM on controller.
- Perfetto native traces were smaller than raw CUPTI but still heavy when recording all cuda APIs.

Sasha: Can we quantify a safe sampling policy to ship? Something like: sample 1 in 1000 requests by default OR sample every 10 minutes for 30s per worker?

Megan: I'd prefer time-based windows per-GPU: every 15 minutes sample for 15s at 1kHz. Plus anomaly-triggered full trace capped to 30s and 200k events. Guardrails:
- Max trace duration 30s
- Max events 200k
- Max disk per-run 1GB
- Auto-delete after 7 days

infra-bot: Implementation notes: need RBAC so only SRE/Perf have access to full traces; store payloads in encrypted S3 prefix with TTL; redact customer prompt data before persisting.

Juan: Also add workload filters at runtime: skip tracing for short sequences (<64 tokens) and small batch sizes (<2). That reduces noise and cost.

Liam: For detecting when to escalate from sampling -> full trace:
- Regression detector: p50/p95 increase > 15% for 3 consecutive windows
- Kernel mismatch heuristic: sampling shows a new hotspot not in baseline
- On-call manual trigger (with guardrail checks)

Megan: Quick command we used to do bounded full trace (dev only):
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx --output=reg_trace \
  --stop=signals:SIGALRM --duration=25
```
Pair with a wrapper that checks output size and aborts if >1GB.

Sasha: Good. A few other practical points:
- Sample-only traces should still capture NVTX spans (lightweight) so we can correlate with request IDs.
- Ensure KV cache timeline sampling: samples must capture KV cache hits vs misses. If not, instrument only the KV cache code path with micro-timers (not full CUPTI).

Juan: Caveat: on older drivers nvprof behavior differs — prefer nsys in prod tooling. nvprof deprecated and less predictable.

Megan: Action items:
- Juan: author a short RFC with default sampling schedule + guardrail numeric limits (due EOD Tue)
- Liam: implement trace size checks + auto-abort in tracing service (PR by end of week)
- Infra: add S3 TTL and RBAC for traces
- Perf team: run A/B on sampling windows (15s@1kHz vs 30s@500Hz) on canary pool and report overhead numbers

Sasha: Thanks. Also add a one-click “safe profile” button in Console that runs the guarded full trace only if the user is in the SRE/perf group and confirms the guardrails.

Megan: noted :ok_hand:

Juan: dropping raw perf snippet from last night (summary): kernel hotspot was a small GEMM at 32x32 that only appears at seq_len>1024. Sampling uncovered it but we needed a 10s full trace to get the timeline and kernel durations.

Sasha: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll keep this as the working thread while RFC lands. If anyone has objections to the numeric guardrails post the RFC draft here.
